chunks: My father (rah) said: It was narrated to me by Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqah from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his forefathers (peace be upon them) that the Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said:
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has decreed Paradise for a young man who used to look frequently in the mirror and thereby praise Allah much.

key_terms.أَوْجَبَ: Has decreed/made obligatory (in the sense of promising)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for a young man who thanks Allah for his beauty?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq narrates that a young man’s frequent gazing into the mirror, coupled with sincere gratitude (shukr) to Allah for his physical attributes, earned him Paradise. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on transforming mundane acts into worship through intention (niyyah) and recognizing divine blessings in one's own creation. It serves as a reminder that gratitude for worldly gifts, when directed solely to Allah, is a pathway to eternal reward.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Abdillah b. Ja’far from Harun b. Muslim from Mas’ada b. Sadaqah from Ja’far b. Muhammad from his forefathers (a.s.) that The Prophet (s.a.w.s.) who said: “
The Almighty Allah has decreed Paradise for those youths who look at the mirror and praise Allah much.”
